item.title: Dick Parry, Saxophonist on Pink Floyd Classics, Dies at 83
item.description:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Today, we're saying goodbye to a music legend. Dick Parry, the iconic saxophonist who worked with Pink Floyd, has passed away at the age of 83.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: The news was shared by David Gilmour, Pink Floyd's guitarist and vocalist, in an emotional tribute on social media. Gilmour and Parry had been friends and collaborators since they were teenagers, playing in local bands around Cambridge.
[Clip of "Money" or "Shine On You Crazy Diamond" plays briefly]
Host: Parry's saxophone solo on Pink Floyd's "The Dark Side of the Moon" and "Wish You Were Here" is unforgettable. His work can be heard on classic songs like "Money" and "Shine On You Crazy Diamond". Gilmour described Parry's playing as "a signature of enormous beauty" that's known to millions.
[Soft music continues]
Host: Born in 1942, Parry's career spanned rock, blues, and jazz. He not only worked with Pink Floyd but also collaborated with other artists like Rory Gallagher, John Entwistle, and Lightnin' Slim.
[Clip of "Wearing the Inside Out" plays briefly]
Host: Even after Pink Floyd, Parry continued to work with Gilmour on solo projects, including "The Division Bell" tour in 1994.
[Soft music fades out]
Host: David Gilmour's tribute to Dick Parry is a heartfelt reminder of the impact Parry had on the music world. We'll miss his iconic saxophone solos, but his legacy will live on through the music he created.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for listening, and we'll catch you in the next episode.
